clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old infant presented with acute onset photophobia, eye blinking, rubbing, irritability, and decreased oral intake. Ophthalmological exam revealed bilateral dendritiform corneal lesions initially raising suspicion for herpetic keratitis. However, conjunctival swab and thumb lesion PCR tests for HSV were negative, excluding herpetic keratitis. Despite valacyclovir treatment, clinical suspicion remained for TYRII due to characteristic ocular findings and plasma amino acid chromatography was performed. The diagnosis of TYRII was confirmed by finding a markedly elevated plasma tyrosine level of 1262 µmol/L (reference range 40–80 µmol/L).
